human_readability_over_density.description: Human readability outranks keyword density. Candidate-facing language is ordinary American English, concrete, direct, and recruiter-natural, with no internal-system jargon, capability stuffing, inflated adjectives, or robotic phrasing.

summary_style.description: The summary is a short natural positioning paragraph connecting current career stage, strongest approved evidence, and target role family. It must not become a keyword inventory.

bullet_style.description: Experience and project bullets prefer action plus context plus outcome/value when evidence supports an outcome; when no defensible outcome exists, use action plus context/purpose without inventing impact. Bullets are kept concise and scan-friendly, normally one to two rendered lines where practical; relevance and clarity matter more than forcing every bullet to the same length.

quantification_discipline.description: Quantification is used when it materially helps the reader understand scale or result and is supported by approved evidence. Numbers are never manufactured merely to make a bullet look stronger.

jd_terminology_use.description: JD terminology may be reused only when the Requirement/EvidenceMatch crosswalk (BLUEPRINT.md Section 140.4) establishes supported overlap. Exact employer terms should be distributed naturally across summary, skills, experience, and project evidence rather than repeated for keyword density.

skills_priority.description: Skills prioritize role-relevant hard skills and evidence-backed operational capabilities. Generic soft-skill filler is excluded unless it is concretely supported by experience evidence.

coherent_narrative.description: The resume tells one coherent early-career story from education and skills into work evidence and project proof, rather than reading as disconnected keyword blocks.

research_basis: U.S. Department of Labor VETS Resume Essentials 2026: targeted achievement statements and job-description keyword alignment
University of Pennsylvania Career Services: 1-2 line bullets, action verbs, context/transferable skills/results, consistent readable formatting
Yale Office of Career Strategy: Action + Project + Result / WHO-style bullets, role-relevant accomplishments, simple ATS-friendly formatting
Indeed 2026 ATS guidance: write for both ATS and recruiter/hiring manager; reuse role-specific job-description keywords naturally
LinkedIn Talent Solutions recruiter guidance: strong organization/format, real achievements, and evidence that matches the role
